title: Toasted Honey Sesame Glaze
description: Freshly ground toasted sesame gives this honey glaze a deeper nutty flavor than sesame oil alone.
equipment: Mortar and pestle or spice grinder

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

steps.title: Toast the sesame
steps.text: Warm {se} in a dry HexClad on low for 1–2 minutes, shaking until pale gold. Grind to a fine powder in a mortar or spice grinder.

steps.title: Emulsify the tahini
steps.text: Whisk {tah}, {ho}, {a}, {ch} and {rv} into the ground sesame until smooth.

steps.title: Warm the glaze
steps.text: Return the mixture to the skillet with {gi} and {so}. Simmer gently for 3 minutes, whisking to prevent sticking.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over moist chicken or soft tofu. The ground sesame stays in the glaze and gives every bite a little roasted flavor.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit the vinegar and ginger. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 78 kcal, 1.3 g protein, 11.8 g total carbohydrate, 3.3 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 102 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 74 kcal, 1.3 g protein, 10.8 g total carbohydrate, 3.3 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 34 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
